chunk_map.heading: H1/lede — "Prep the run, fill the gaps"
Phase 1: Pick the task you'll send off
Push back until the task is one end-to-end slice
Phase 2: Build the ranked list of what will hurt the agent
Correct the list and reprioritise it
Fill the worst two or three gaps
Match each fill to its shape and home
Push back when Claude drifts from the codebase

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.

rules_evaluated.evidence: No chunk points at another file by position; "next module" forward-teases (chunk 2 line 49, chunk 5 line 79) name no file and no location, so §2 (which governs positional pointers, not generic future-teasing) has no candidate here.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No "the X you did/saw/caught" construction appears anywhere in the body; nothing to resolve against the module's exercise set.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: File contains no guess-before-reveal / predict-then-watch beat.

Every chunk carries at least one self-standing directive (e.g. chunk 2 "Push back when the screen misses something...", chunk 4 "Tell it what's wrong, what's missing, and what you'd move up."); none is a bare wait-state.

chunk 7 "Push back when Claude drifts from the codebase": line 104 header, but lines 108 and 110 ("Time check" blockquote and "Before the send-off, tidy the folder") are unrelated to pushing back on drift — a reader who projects only the header would not expect a pacing callout and a tidy-up instruction bundled under it. Harm check: the harm rule 6 guards against is a header that misdescribes what the slide actually says, so a trainer glancing at deck order or a student skimming headers gets a false preview; here two of the chunk's three beats fall outside what the header promises, so the harm is present, not just the rule's shape matching.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Either split the time-check + tidy-up into their own chunk/heading, or broaden the header to name the closing beat generally (e.g. a header naming "close out the fill" rather than only "push back").

rules_evaluated.evidence: Checked each sub-item across all chunks: no "Not X. Not Y. Z." construction; no anaphora/epistrophe triple; no self-grading superlative (value-prop leak) in the body; no number-with-retraction; no abstraction-noun stack; no verb triplet with an empty leg. None of the six sub-item shapes appear.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No repo/maintainer vocabulary (surface-as-noun, firing, compendium, forcing function, beat, mood, Connections-as-proper-noun) appears in any chunk; tool names (Agent tool, AskUserQuestion) and file paths are ordinary engineering references, not dialect.

No bullet-lead bold monoculture found elsewhere.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content — verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
